ledger.claim: The driver's reroute was not traffic-justified, so the case cannot be disposed of on the footing that he was reacting to conditions on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The only traffic record in the file is the LTA advisory for the recommended corridor — Tampines Expressway (TPE) between Tampines Avenue 7 and PIE, towards PIE, valid 07:59 to 09:29 on the morning of 10 September 2026, which covers the whole trip window — and it carries type NONE, records 'no incident, roadwork or closure' and speed bands 4-5 throughout. The driver's statement that the TPE exit to PIE 'got queue' is therefore a bare assertion, and POL-RD-23 says a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The platform's own events (route_deviation_detected at 08:40:24 at the TPE/Tampines Avenue 7 exit, route_rejoined at 08:48:22 at Simei Avenue), and the 41 trace fixes running down Tampines Avenue 7 and Simei Avenue, show a deliberate departure from the recommended route that no recorded condition explains.

The driver also failed the notice obligation POL-RD-21 places on any reroute: he had to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log for TRP-05018 is contiguous and holds 0 messages (it matches trip_record.chat_message_count), and the trip record holds no in-app calls at all, so neither route to notice exists in the record; the driver's statement, filed at 18:37 on the day in answer to the rider's complaint, is not notice given at the time of the deviation. With no chat message, no call and no recording, the rider's acknowledgment cannot be shown, and under POL-RD-21 the deviation cannot be treated as agreed.

On the figures the policy makes the measure, the rider was carried 12.8 km against a 12.0 km recommended route — an excess of 0.80 km, which at this trip's 0.72 SGD per km rate is 0.58 SGD under POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula (no surge) — and the detour ran eight minutes off the expressway through Tampines Avenue 7 and Simei Avenue, from 08:40:24 to 08:48:22, all of it metered. The rider's side does not put its case on the '4 km' figure or the Google Maps comparison in the complaint, because POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation by the platform's recorded distances and forbids re-measuring from the trace; it puts its case on the recorded 0.80 km, on the total absence of any traffic justification for it under POL-RD-23, and on the total absence of any notice to the rider under POL-RD-21.

The deviation on this trip is 0.80 km, far below the 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as the platform's recorded actual distance minus the platform's recorded recommended distance (12.8 km - 12.0 km = 0.80 km), and expressly says the GPS trace is not used to re-measure the distance. The rider's figure of '4 km out of the way' has no support anywhere in the record.

Because 0.80 km is within POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, POL-RD-24 row (e) applies - not traffic-justified, deviation of 1 km or less - and the answer is no refund: the present charge stands and the rider's claim fails (NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03).

The outcome does not depend on how the traffic question falls. If the reroute were held traffic-justified, POL-RD-24 row (c) - traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less - also returns NO_ACTION. Both live branches of the matrix give the same result for this trip, so the driver keeps the metered fare either way.

In fact the reroute is not traffic-justified on this record: the LTA advisory for the TPE towards PIE segment carries type NONE, which is not one of the kinds POL-RD-23 names (closure, congestion, incident), and its own text records no incident, roadwork or closure and speed bands 4-5 through the window. The driver's account of a queue at the TPE/PIE exit is therefore uncorroborated - but as the matrix above shows, the driver does not need it.

Even on the branch of POL-RD-24 that would pay money, the amount is the excess distance fare: the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent. That is 0.80 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.58 SGD. The 5.00 SGD the rider asks for corresponds to no measure the policy provides, and the trip's own ledger shows refund_issued_sgd of 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation: EV-CHAT-05018 is a contiguous chat log with 0 entries and the trip record carries an empty in_app_calls list, so POL-RD-21's notice obligation is not met on this record and no acknowledgment by the rider can be established. I concede that point. It does not move the outcome, because POL-RD-24 makes the notice material only where the deviation is over 1 km (row (b)); at 0.80 km this case sits in the tolerance rows, where notice is not an ingredient.

The rider asks the tribunal to infer from the driver's history that 'he does it to everyone'. POL-GEN-01 permits only rider_profile.fraud_flags and driver_profile.fraud_flags (for POL-GEN-22) and rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d (for POL-NS-25) to be cited; a driver's deviation_flags_90d, prior_no_show_flags and no_show_terminations_30d are context only and may never establish a fact about this trip or decide it. This trip must be decided on its own evidence, and that evidence shows 0.80 km.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider asked for $5.00 back, saying the driver went about 4 km out of the way. The policy does not measure the deviation that way. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the platform's recorded actual distance minus its recorded recommended distance, and the GPS trace is expressly not used to re-measure it: 12.8 km minus 12.0 km = 0.80 km. That is within the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the refund matrix in POL-RD-24 places this trip in a tolerance row, not a refund row. On the traffic question, the only traffic record in the file is the LTA advisory for the recommended corridor (TPE towards PIE, covering the trip window); it carries type NONE, records no incident, roadwork or closure, and its own text shows speed bands 4-5, so the reroute was not traffic-justified and POL-RD-23 is not satisfied. That gives row (e) of the matrix (not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less): no refund, within tolerance. The result is the same if the traffic question fell the other way, because row (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less) also returns no refund, so nothing turns on the driver's account of a queue at the TPE/PIE exit. The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation - EV-CHAT-05018 is a contiguous log with 0 messages and the trip record shows no in-app calls - and that failure is accepted under POL-RD-21; but notice enters the matrix only where the deviation exceeds 1 km (row (b)), so at 0.80 km it does not change the outcome. The rider's suggestion that the driver 'does it to everyone' cannot be used: POL-GEN-01 makes driver_profile fields such as deviation_flags_90d, prior_no_show_flags and no_show_terminations_30d context only, incapable of establishing anything about this trip. All five artifacts relied on are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, traffic advisory), so no impairment discount applies and there is no gap requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26. The $0.58 excess-distance figure the driver cites (0.80 km x $0.72/km, POL-RD-24) is not reached, because no matrix row pays money on a deviation within tolerance, and the $5.00 the rider asks for corresponds to no measure the policy provides. The contested value is $5.00, below POL-GEN-22's $10.00 band, so this AI ruling is final at any confidence, and it also meets POL-RD-25's 0.80 requirement (neither profile carries a fraud flag). The present charge stands.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
